Definition: first person singular of a past tense of G3784; I ought (wish), i.e. (interjection) oh that!:--would (to God).
BiblicalUsage: Oh that! This is the word of a wish that cannot be helped. Paul says, now ye are full, now ye are rich, would to God ye did reign, and he wishes the Corinthians could bear with his folly a little.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word catches the longing of a shepherd's heart: Paul wishes his people were already reigning with Christ, and that wish still aches in me.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
